title: Responses streaming sanitizer + toolcall handshake + seed/metadata passthrough
author: Anya Patel
description:
Motivation: Customers using the OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoints reported two classes of issues in high-concurrency streaming scenarios: (1) reassembled chunks occasionally produce malformed JSON for structured outputs when fragments arrive out of order, and (2) tool/function-call handshakes (tool metadata + trigger signals) are sometimes lost when intermediary proxies rewrite streaming frames. This PR introduces a lightweight 'stream sanitizer' in the OpenAI-bridge layer and a small protocol handshake for tool/function calls to ensure deterministic seed passthrough and opaque metadata forwarding across the bridge.

What this does (single-line summary): adds stable chunk framing/sequence validation, emits tool-handshake events to guarantee toolcall integrity, and forwards client-supplied seed/determinism and arbitrary metadata through the bridge without mutation.

Key changes (design notes): - Stream sanitizer: attaches sequence ids and checksums to streaming frame envelopes within the bridge. Frames that fail validation trigger a deterministic re-request path (soft-retry) or out-of-order buffering with a bounded window (configurable via runtime flag STREAM_SANITIZER_WINDOW_MS). This reduces JSON reassembly errors for structured outputs. - Toolcall handshake: introduces a brief "tool-ready" / "tool-accept" event pair in the streaming protocol used only between bridge and runtime; this is backward-compatible because clients that do not implement the new events will still receive final toolcall events (handshake is honored internally). - Seed & determinism passthrough: any incoming seed/rng_hint fields from OpenAI-style requests are preserved in the request context and propagated to the runtime and any downstream model variants. We add an explicit metadata header (X-Redwood-Rng-Hint) in the bridge-to-runtime path. - Metadata passthrough: arbitrary top-level request metadata is now passed through the bridge unchanged (we treat it as opaque key:value pairs and log a sanitized subset for observability). - Structured output preservation: the sanitizer treats codeblock/JSON tokens specially (preserve token boundaries when possible) and validates JSON well-formedness at reassembly time; if reassembly fails we emit a stable error object that clients can detect and optionally request a fallback sync response.

Compatibility & rollout: - Feature guarded behind a runtime config flag (enabled-by-default in staging, opt-in on older Dedicated stacks). - Backward compatibility: bridge will not drop frames for older clients; it falls back to streaming passthrough if the client signals legacy compatibility header (X-Redwood-Legacy-Resp). - Migration: docs/compatibility/resp-streaming-migration.md added to the docs site; SDKs updated to expose the new seed passthrough header in Python/TS.

Testing & validation: - Unit tests for envelope framing and checksum validation (bridge tests). - Integration tests: end-to-end toolcall flows including a mock external tool and JSON-structured outputs. - Load/perf: perf-canary run included; sanitizer added ~1.8% p99 latency in worst-case synthetic fragmentation but eliminated ~95% of JSON reassembly failures. - Canary plan: staged rollout: canary -> region -> global over 72h with automated rollback on error-rate threshold (see rollout section in description).

Checklist: - [x] Add stream sanitizer implementation and tests - [x] Implement tool-handshake events and adapters - [x] Propagate rng/seed hints through bridge -> runtime - [x] Add docs and migration guide - [x] Update Python/TS SDK headers to expose passthrough hint - [x] Canary and perf runs completed

Merge notes: squash merge to preserve a single logical change. See release notes at the bottom for customer-facing summary.
commits: feat(bridge): add stream envelope framing and checksum validation
feat(bridge): implement out-of-order buffering window and soft-retry path
feat(api): toolcall handshake events (tool-ready/tool-accept) in responses adapter
feat(runtime): accept X-Redwood-Rng-Hint and pass to model execution context
fix(tests): add deterministic fixtures for streaming fragmentation
docs: add resp-streaming-migration.md and SDK header examples
chore: bump integration-harness and update perf-canary config
review_comments: Samuel Irving: Can you clarify how the bounded buffer window prevents head-of-line blocking under very high fragmentation? If the window is too large we risk memory blowup.

Author (Anya Patel): Buffer window is strictly bounded and measured in ms; we also limit per-client buffer size. Added config STREAM_SANITIZER_MAX_FRAMES to avoid OOM; added tests in stream_sanitizer_test.go to simulate pathological fragmentation.
Renee Cho: LGTMed overall. Please add a small migration note for Dedicated customers so they can opt-out during upgrade.
Author (Anya Patel): Added docs/compatibility/resp-streaming-migration.md and a short section in release_notes. Also wired in config toggle for Dedicated upgrades.
Diego Alvarez: Noted ~2% p99 impact on synthetic perf runs. Can you add an opt-out flag for latency-sensitive routes?
Author (Anya Patel): Added route-level opt-out via route.annotations["resp.streaming.sanitize"] = false; updated console docs and tests.
release_notes: Responses streaming reliability: bridge-level stream sanitizer and toolcall handshake. Preserves OpenAI-style seed/determinism hints and forwards arbitrary request metadata. This reduces structured-output reassembly errors and makes tool/function calling more resilient across proxies. Rolling update with opt-outs for latency-sensitive routes.
body_summary: Implements stream framing + checksum validation, tool-handshake events, seed passthrough header, metadata passthrough, tests, docs, and staged canary rollout. Backwards-compatible by falling back to legacy passthrough when requested.
